active_paradigms.idea: Remove the reflection constraint and solve one full epigraph nonlinear program with SLSQP from a fixed asymmetric active-set seed.
active_paradigms.description: The current program obtains its score by differential evolution over an 11-variable reflection-symmetric family, followed by a symmetric SLSQP polish; its useful features are exact feasibility decoding, direct evaluation of all 165 triples, and an epigraph variable for the minimum area. Its principal limitation is that reflection symmetry reduces the 22-coordinate placement problem to only 11 degrees of freedom and can exclude the true 11-point optimum. Replace this with one direct SLSQP solve over all 11 Cartesian points plus threshold t, starting from one fixed, hand-stored asymmetric perturbation of the present best layout. Use constraints |det(pj-pi,pk-pi)|/sqrt(3)-t >= 0 for every triple, plus the four linear triangle-membership inequalities for every point. Supply the analytic Jacobian, but compute its determinant sign separately for every triple at the current iterate, as the current code already does. Preserve boundary-active points in the seed, but perturb paired points independently so that the optimizer is able to discover unequal side spacings and unequal interior heights. Use bounds x in [0,1], y in [0,h], t in [0,0.1], maxiter around 3000, and a tight ftol. Return the directly recomputed candidate only if it is feasible and improves a literal safe fallback layout.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized. This specifically attacks the likely score ceiling caused by enforced mirror symmetry; evaluation time remains acceptable if the final result is hard-coded after discovery or if one local solve is retained.
active_paradigms.cautions: This must be a single direct SLSQP call, not DE followed by SLSQP. Absolute determinants are nonsmooth only at collinearity; initialize from a layout with all determinants safely nonzero and validate the final minimum directly rather than trusting t. Avoid the current dead unrestricted optimizer block: it is unreachable because the function returns before it.

active_paradigms.idea: Use deterministic DIRECT global search on a boundary-class, but asymmetric, barycentric parameterization.
active_paradigms.description: The existing DE stage is global but searches a symmetric 11-dimensional model and expends substantial work on a stochastic population; moreover, the later local polish cannot leave that symmetry class. Build a deterministic reduced geometric model with two independently positioned points on each of the three sides and five unconstrained interior points, giving 16 continuous parameters without imposing reflection symmetry. Decode side coordinates directly by their side fraction and decode each interior point using nested barycentric coordinates, so every point is feasible for every box vector. Define the objective as the negative minimum normalized area across all 165 triples, with no separate feasibility penalty needed. Call DIRECT once with `locally_biased=False` initially, or `True` if runtime is restrictive, using eps around 1e-5, maxfun selected from the evaluation limit, and a fixed deterministic initial domain. Unlike DE, DIRECT systematically subdivides promising boxes and is reproducible without a random population, which is valuable for a highly nonsmooth lower-envelope objective. The side-class model retains the boundary structure that makes the current solution strong while allowing the three sides and the interior configuration to become genuinely asymmetric. After an offline successful run, embed the returned coordinates as constants so evaluator execution is effectively instantaneous.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized, emphasizing escape from both the reflection restriction and DE population/basin dependence. Hard-coding the discovered layout also minimizes eval_time.
active_paradigms.cautions: DIRECT suffers from dimension growth, so do not use unrestricted 22 Cartesian variables; the 6-boundary-plus-5-interior parameterization is essential. Ensure no class forces three points onto one straight side: exactly two points per side is safe. DIRECT availability depends on the installed SciPy version, so retain a precomputed literal-point fallback if it is unavailable.

active_paradigms.idea: Formulate a one-call mixed-integer grid-selection maximin model to discover asymmetric combinatorial scaffolds before freezing the coordinates.
active_paradigms.description: The central difficulty is not merely continuous polishing: it is identifying which points belong on which sides and which triples are active, and the current reflected DE representation fixes these choices too early. Construct a nonuniform candidate set inside the triangle containing dense points along all three boundaries, near-boundary offset rows, and several interior barycentric rows, deliberately without reflection pairing. Use one binary variable per candidate point, require exactly 11 selected points, and maximize continuous t. For every candidate triple (i,j,k), add the valid big-M inequality t <= A_ijk + M(3-bi-bj-bk), where A_ijk is that fixed triple's normalized area and M is a proven upper bound such as 1. This enforces the objective only when all three vertices of a triple are selected; it exactly matches the evaluator on the finite candidate pool. Solve this single MILP with HiGHS, inspect the selected asymmetric scaffold, and, for the submitted constructor, return the selected coordinates as a literal constant array. A carefully designed multiresolution candidate pool can capture unequal side spacings that continuous symmetric search never considers and produces a deterministic O(1) submitted function. Use the MILP as an offline discovery method rather than paying its solve time during every evaluation.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The discrete structural component of min_area_normalized: side membership, number of boundary points, and active-triple incidence. The final hard-coded output gives negligible eval_time.
active_paradigms.cautions: The number of triple constraints grows cubically, so start with roughly 50-90 geometrically meaningful candidates rather than a uniform fine grid. Use exact or high-precision precomputed areas and a conservative M; too-small M incorrectly cuts feasible selections, while very-large M weakens the relaxation. A plain triangular lattice contains many collinear triples, but the model can avoid selecting all three; include staggered offset rows to make competitive noncollinear selections possible.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use reflection-symmetric parameterization with scipy.optimize.differential_evolution to globally optimize the true maximin geometry
tried_paradigms.description: The current program uses a 22-coordinate epigraph SLSQP formulation, with 29 sequential local solves, so it is vulnerable to local active-set basins and spends most of its time repeatedly polishing mediocre layouts. Impose only left-right reflection symmetry about x=0.5: represent five points in the left half, their five reflected partners, and one point on the symmetry axis, giving exactly 11 points with roughly half the continuous degrees of freedom. Parameterize every free point by triangle-safe barycentric or nested coordinates, so every candidate is feasible without a domain penalty. Optimize the evaluator's actual quantity, namely the minimum of all 165 unsigned doubled determinants divided by sqrt(3), rather than relying on an auxiliary epigraph variable. Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once with a fixed seed, substantial population size, mutation dithering, and workers=1 for determinism. Seed its initial population around a hand-designed six-boundary-point scaffold as well as broad samples in the reduced coordinate box. This is fundamentally more global than the present SLSQP restarts and symmetry removes many equivalent permutations/reflections that confuse unconstrained search. Return the best decoded candidate directly, after clipping only by an inward epsilon to avoid evaluator-boundary roundoff.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized; the reduced symmetry search is intended to escape the approximately 0.026 normalized-area local basin represented by the current 0.711 combined score. Runtime is controlled by reducing the dimension from 22 to about 11 and making exactly one global optimizer call.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Reflection symmetry is a powerful restriction but must be tested against an asymmetric stored fallback, since the global n=11 optimum is not guaranteed to be reflection symmetric. Do not use a discontinuous infeasibility penalty: use a feasibility-preserving coordinate decode. The raw min is nonsmooth, so use a sufficiently large population and iteration budget rather than relying on local polish. Every reflected point must remain distinct from its axis partner and all 165 areas must still be recomputed before return.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve a fixed geometric active-set KKT system with scipy.optimize.root instead of asking SLSQP to discover it
tried_paradigms.description: The current SLSQP objective is linear in its epigraph variable while every area constraint contains an absolute determinant, producing kinks whenever a triangle changes orientation and often causing premature termination at a nonoptimal active set. A stronger construction is to first identify, offline during development, the small set of triangles that are tight in a high-quality candidate and the points fixed on each outer side. Encode that hypothesized contact graph directly: each active triangle supplies a signed determinant equation equal to a common target doubled area, boundary contacts supply line equations, and remaining equations are stationarity equations from the maximin KKT conditions using nonnegative multiplier variables. Call scipy.optimize.root once from embedded high-precision approximate coordinates, target area, and multiplier estimates. This directly solves the smooth algebraic branch on which the best arrangement lies rather than repeatedly optimizing a nonsmooth minimum. Normalize signed orientation choices once from the incumbent so determinant equations have no abs kinks. After the root solve, independently evaluate every one of the 165 actual unsigned areas and return the result only if it is triangle-feasible and improves the embedded certified fallback. This can yield a substantial final improvement when the main deficiency is SLSQP's inaccurate active-constraint balancing rather than the family of the configuration.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized, especially final high-precision equalization of the bottleneck triangles. It also minimizes eval_time because a single small deterministic nonlinear-system call replaces 29 SLSQP starts plus continuation.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This requires careful offline active-set discovery; an omitted triangle can become smaller than the proposed common threshold, so full evaluator-equivalent verification is essential. The equation count must equal the number of primal coordinates, common area variable, and retained KKT multipliers; remove redundant equal-area equations or add an explicit gauge/contact condition. Reject roots with negative multipliers, wrong determinant signs, duplicate points, or any point outside the triangle. Keep a static feasible numerical layout as a fallback because root may converge to another algebraic branch.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.shgo on a low-dimensional structured boundary/interior family to obtain basin-certified global candidates
tried_paradigms.description: The existing program has a useful insight—strong candidates use two points on each side and five interior points—but then releases all 22 coordinates, losing the structural information and making every SLSQP run highly nonconvex. Retain that family explicitly with six side parameters and a compact set of interior barycentric parameters, optionally tying selected interiors by reflection or rotational relations chosen from a geometric drawing. Express side locations in open intervals and interior positions via barycentric coordinates, so feasibility is automatic. Define a direct maximin objective from all 165 triangle areas, using a smooth log-sum-exp lower-envelope surrogate only if necessary for topology construction, and evaluate the exact min at returned candidates. Make one scipy.optimize.shgo call with deterministic Sobol sampling, bounds on the reduced parameters, and an appropriately small number of local iterations. SHGO's simplicial homology exploration is qualitatively different from random SLSQP starts: it deliberately locates multiple separated basins and returns the best one under a single optimization invocation. The best structured solution can then be embedded as constants in the final constructor if it outperforms the current dynamically optimized output.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized through systematic exploration of the promising six-side-point geometry; secondary eval_time through a low-dimensional model rather than 22-variable repeated local solves.
tried_paradigms.cautions: SHGO is not suitable for the full unconstrained 22-dimensional representation, so the geometric parameterization is essential. Overconstraining the interior pattern can exclude the optimum; compare several fixed families offline, but the submitted constructor should invoke only one selected SHGO model or simply return its precomputed result. The exact minimum is nonsmooth, so use robust sampling density and always choose by exact area, not merely the surrogate. Ensure parameter bounds prevent coincident side points and preserve an inward margin for floating-point feasibility.
